text.p: These are the leading stories in the Mozambican press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Four of the major cotton companies in Mozambique have demanded that the government lower the statutory minimum price they pay to peasant producers. Since December 1995 the minimum price has been the equivalent of about 35 US cents per kg.

- An attempt by the opposition Renamo party to increase the number of towns where municipal elections are to be held later this year was defeated in parliament. The government bill includes 33 towns, while Renamo's failed amendment called for 28 to be added.
